title.zh: 卷一百三十五 列傳第七十三: 外國下 高麗 金國語解 官稱 人事 物象 物類 姓氏
title.en: Volume 135 Biographies 73: Foreign Countries 2: Goryeo, Explanation of the Language of the State of Jin, Official Titles, Human Affairs, Art, Classes of Objects, Family Names
title.raw: 卷一百三十五 列傳第七十三: 外國下 高麗 金國語解 官稱 人事 物象 物類 姓氏 Volume 135 Biographies 73: Foreign Countries 2: Goryeo, Explanation of the Language of the State of Jin, Official Titles, Human Affairs, Art, Classes of Objects, Family Names

sentences.zh: 外國下

translations.literal: Foreign Countries, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Foreign States, Continued

sentences.zh: 高麗國王，王楷。

translations.literal: The king of the state of Goryeo was Wang Kai.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goryeo was Wang Kai.

sentences.zh: 其地鴨綠江以東，曷懶路以南，東南皆至於海。

translations.literal: Its land lay east of the Yalu River and south of the Halin Route; to the southeast it reached the sea on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory extended east of the Yalu River and south of the Halin Route, with the southeast bounded entirely by the sea.

sentences.zh: 自遼時，歲時遣使修貢，事具《遼史》。

translations.literal: From the time of the Liao, each year envoys were sent to present tribute; the matter is fully recorded in the 《History of Liao》.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Liao period it had sent annual tribute missions; the details are given in the 《History of Liao》.

sentences.zh: 唐初，靺鞨有粟末、黑水兩部，皆臣屬於高麗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tang, among the Mohe there were the two divisions of Sumo and Heishui, both of which were subject to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tang, the Mohe were divided into the Sumo and Heishui branches, both of which acknowledged Goryeo as their overlord.

sentences.zh: 唐滅高麗，粟末保東牟山漸強大，號渤海，姓大氏，有文物禮樂。

translations.literal: When the Tang destroyed Goryeo, the Sumo, holding Dongmoushan, gradually grew powerful, styled themselves Bohai, took the surname Da, and possessed culture, rites, and music.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang conquered Goryeo, the Sumo Mohe who held Dongmoushan grew steadily stronger, proclaimed the state of Bohai under the Da clan, and developed a full court culture with rites and music.

sentences.zh: 至唐末稍衰，自後不復有聞。

translations.literal: By the end of the Tang it had declined somewhat, and thereafter nothing more was heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Tang it had begun to wane, and after that it vanished from the record.

sentences.zh: 金伐遼，渤海來歸，蓋其遺裔也。

translations.literal: When the Jin attacked the Liao, Bohai came to submit; they were probably its surviving descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin campaigned against the Liao, the Bohai submitted—they were likely descendants of that former state.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨居古肅慎地，有山曰白山，蓋長白山，金國之所起焉。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe dwelt in the ancient land of the Sushen; there was a mountain called Baishan, which was probably Changbaishan, where the state of Jin had its rise.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe inhabited the old territory of the Sushen. They had a mountain called White Mountain—likely Changbai Mountain—where the Jin state had its origins.

sentences.zh: 女直雖舊屬高麗，不復相通者久矣。

translations.literal: Although the Jurchen had formerly been subject to Goryeo, they had long ceased to have contact.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen had once been under Goryeo's sway, but the two peoples had been out of contact for a long time.

sentences.zh: 及金滅遼，高麗以事遼舊禮稱臣于金。

translations.literal: When the Jin destroyed the Liao, Goryeo, following the old ceremonies used toward the Liao, declared itself a vassal of the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin overthrew the Liao, Goryeo acknowledged Jin suzerainty using the same ceremonial forms it had formerly observed toward the Liao.

sentences.zh: 初，有醫者善治疾，本高麗人，不知其始自何而來，亦不著其姓名，居女直之完顏部。

translations.literal: At first there was a physician skilled at treating illness; he was originally a man of Goryeo, but it was not known whence he had first come, nor was his name recorded. He lived among the Wanyan clan of the Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: Early on there was a physician renowned for his skill. A native of Goryeo, he had come from parts unknown and left no name in the record; he settled among the Wanyan Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 穆宗時戚屬有疾，此醫者診視之，穆宗謂醫者曰：「汝能使此人病癒，則吾遣人送汝歸汝鄉國。」

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Muzong a kinsman fell ill; this physician examined and treated him. Muzong said to the physician, "If you can cure this person's illness, I shall send someone to escort you back to your native country."
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Muzong a royal kinsman fell ill, and this physician was called to treat him. Muzong told the physician, "If you can cure him, I will have you escorted home to your own country."

sentences.zh: 醫者曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The physician said, "I agree."
translations.idiomatic: The physician answered, "I shall."

sentences.zh: 其人疾果愈，穆宗乃以初約歸之。

translations.literal: That person's illness was indeed cured, and Muzong thereupon fulfilled the original promise and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: The patient recovered, and Muzong honored his original promise and sent the physician home.

sentences.zh: 乙離骨嶺僕散部胡石來勃堇居高麗、女直之兩間，穆宗使族人叟阿招之，因使叟阿送醫者，歸之高麗境上。

translations.literal: Hushilai, a tribal chief of the Pusan division at Yiliguri Ridge, dwelt between Goryeo and the Jurchen. Muzong sent his clansman Sou'a to summon him, and also had Sou'a escort the physician back to the Goryeo border.
translations.idiomatic: Hushilai, a Pusan chieftain at Yiliguri Ridge, lived between Goryeo and Jurchen territory. Muzong dispatched his kinsman Sou'a to summon him and, at the same time, to escort the physician back to the Goryeo frontier.

sentences.zh: 醫者歸至高麗，因謂高麗人，女直居黑水部者部族日強，兵益精悍，年穀屢稔。

translations.literal: When the physician returned to Goryeo, he told the people of Goryeo that among the Jurchen dwelling in the Heishui division the clans were growing stronger day by day, their troops ever more fierce, and their harvests repeatedly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Goryeo, the physician warned the court that the Jurchen of the Heishui branch were growing stronger by the day, their warriors ever more formidable, and their harvests consistently plentiful.

sentences.zh: 高麗王聞之。

translations.literal: The king of Goryeo heard this.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goryeo took heed of this report.

sentences.zh: 乃通使於女直。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened communications with the Jurchen by sending envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly dispatched envoys to establish contact with the Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 既而，胡石來來歸，遂率乙離骨嶺東諸部皆內附。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Hushilai came to submit, and then led all the tribes east of Yiliguri Ridge to attach themselves inward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hushilai submitted in person, and all the tribes east of Yiliguri Ridge followed him into Jurchen allegiance.

sentences.zh: 穆宗十年癸未，阿疏自遼使其徒達紀來說曷懶甸人，曷懶甸人執之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Muzong, guisi year, Ashu, on behalf of the Liao, sent his follower Daji to win over the people of the Halin district; the people of Halin seized him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Muzong, guisi year, Ashu, acting for the Liao, sent his man Daji to win over the Halin district people, but they seized him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以達紀送高麗，謂高麗王曰：「前此為亂於汝鄙者，皆此輩也。」

translations.literal: Muzong sent Daji to Goryeo and said to the king of Goryeo, "Those who have been causing disorder in your borderlands before this are all of this sort."
translations.idiomatic: Muzong handed Daji over to Goryeo, telling the king, "The men who have been raiding your frontier are exactly this sort of people."

sentences.zh: 及破蕭海里，使斡魯罕往高麗報捷，高麗亦使使來賀。

translations.literal: After defeating Xiao Haili, he sent Woluhan to Goryeo to report the victory, and Goryeo also sent envoys to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of Xiao Haili, he sent Woluhan to Goryeo with news of the victory, and Goryeo returned the courtesy with congratulatory envoys.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複使斜葛與斡魯罕往聘，高麗王曰：「斜葛，女直之族弟也，其禮有加矣。」

translations.literal: Before long he again sent Xiege and Woluhan on a friendly mission. The king of Goryeo said, "Xiege is a clansman younger brother of the Jurchen; his reception should be enhanced."
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he sent Xiege and Woluhan on another mission. The Goryeo king remarked, "Xiege is a junior kinsman of the Jurchen chiefs—let his reception be especially generous."

sentences.zh: 乃以一大銀盤為謝。

translations.literal: He thereupon presented a large silver platter as a gift of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a large silver platter in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 厥後，曷懶甸諸部盡欲來附，高麗聞之不欲使來附，恐近於己而不利也，使人邀止之。

translations.literal: Thereafter all the tribes of the Halin district wished to come and attach themselves, but when Goryeo heard of this it did not wish them to submit, fearing that their proximity would be disadvantageous, and sent men to intercept and stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward every Halin tribe sought to submit to the Jurchen. Goryeo, fearing that their proximity would work against its interests, sent men to block them.

sentences.zh: 斜葛在高麗及往來曷懶道中，具知其事，遂使石適歡往納曷懶甸人。

translations.literal: Xiege, while in Goryeo and traveling the road to and from Halin, learned the full story of the affair, and thereupon had Shi Shihuan go to receive the people of the Halin district.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege learned the full story while in Goryeo and on the Halin road, and sent Shi Shihuan to bring the Halin tribes in.

sentences.zh: 未行而穆宗沒，康宗嗣，遣石適歡以星顯統門之兵往至乙離骨嶺，益募兵趨活涅水，徇地曷懶甸，收叛亡七城。

translations.literal: Before he set out Muzong died and Kangzong succeeded. He dispatched Shi Shihuan with troops from Xingxian and Tongmen as far as Yiliguri Ridge, recruited more soldiers, pressed toward the Huonie River, marched through the Halin district, and recovered seven cities of defectors and fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shi Shihuan could march, Muzong died and Kangzong took the throne. Kangzong sent him with troops from Xingxian and Tongmen to Yiliguri Ridge, raised additional forces, advanced to the Huonie River, swept the Halin district, and recovered seven rebel-held towns.

sentences.zh: 高麗使人來告曰：「事有當議者。」

translations.literal: Goryeo sent envoys to report, saying, "There are matters that ought to be discussed."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent envoys with a message: "There are matters that require discussion."

sentences.zh: 曷懶甸官屬使斜勒詳穩、冶剌保詳穩往，石適歡亦使杯魯往，高麗執冶剌保等，而遣杯魯曰：「無與爾事。」

translations.literal: The officials of the Halin district sent Xiele Xiangwen and Yelibao Xiangwen; Shi Shihuan also sent Peilu. Goryeo seized Yelibao and the others, but sent Peilu back, saying, "This has nothing to do with you."
translations.idiomatic: Halin officials dispatched Xiele Xiangwen and Yelibao Xiangwen, while Shi Shihuan sent Peilu. Goryeo detained Yelibao and his party but sent Peilu back with the words, "This is none of your concern."

sentences.zh: 於是，五水之民皆附於高麗，團練使陷者十四人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people of the Five Waters all attached themselves to Goryeo, and fourteen regimental commanders were taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the Five Waters peoples all went over to Goryeo, and fourteen regimental commanders fell into captivity.

sentences.zh: 二年甲申，高麗來攻，石適歡大破之，殺獲甚眾，追入其境，焚略其戍守而還。

translations.literal: In the second year, jiashen year, Goryeo came to attack; Shi Shihuan inflicted a great defeat, killing and capturing in great numbers, pursued into their territory, burned and plundered their garrisons, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, jiashen year, Goryeo attacked. Shi Shihuan routed them with heavy casualties, pursued into their territory, burned their frontier posts, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 四月，高麗複來攻，石適歡以五百人禦于辟登水，複大破之，追入辟登水，逐其殘眾逾境。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Goryeo attacked again; Shi Shihuan with five hundred men met them at the Bideng River, again inflicted a great defeat, pursued into the Bideng River, and drove their scattered remnants beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Goryeo attacked again. With five hundred men Shi Shihuan met them at the Bideng River, won another crushing victory, pursued them into the river, and drove the survivors beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 於是，高麗王曰：「告邊釁者皆官屬祥丹、傍都里、昔畢罕輩也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the king of Goryeo said, "Those who reported the border provocations were all officials—Xiangdan, Bangduli, Xibihan, and the like."
translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo king then said, "The border incidents were the work of officials—Xiangdan, Bangduli, Xibihan, and their associates."

sentences.zh: 十四團練、六路使人在高麗者，皆歸之，遣使來請和。

translations.literal: The fourteen regimental commanders and the commissioners of the six routes who were in Goryeo were all returned, and envoys were sent to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the fourteen regimental commanders and the six-route commissioners held in Goryeo and sent envoys to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 遂使斜葛經正疆界，至乙離骨水、曷懶甸活禰水，留之兩月。

translations.literal: He then sent Xiege to survey and rectify the border, as far as the Yiliguri River and the Huonie River of the Halin district, and kept him there for two months.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege was then sent to demarcate the border as far as the Yiliguri and Halin Huonie rivers, and remained on the task for two months.

sentences.zh: 斜葛不能聽訟，每一事輒至枝蔓，民頗苦之。

translations.literal: Xiege was unable to hear lawsuits; every case tended to branch out endlessly, and the people suffered considerably from this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege proved incapable of adjudicating disputes—every case sprawled into endless complications, and the people found it burdensome.

sentences.zh: 康宗召斜葛還，而遣石適歡往。

translations.literal: Kangzong recalled Xiege and sent Shi Shihuan in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong recalled Xiege and replaced him with Shi Shihuan.

sentences.zh: 石適歡立幕府于三潺水，其嘗陰與高麗往來為亂階者，即正其罪，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Shi Shihuan established his headquarters at the Sanchan River; those who had secretly communicated with Goryeo and become agents of disorder were immediately punished according to their crimes, while the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shihuan set up headquarters at the Sanchan River, punished only those who had secretly colluded with Goryeo to stir up trouble, and left everyone else unmolested.

sentences.zh: 康宗以為能。

translations.literal: Kangzong considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 四年丙戌，高麗使使黑歡方石來賀嗣位，康宗使杯魯報聘，且尋前約，取亡命之民，高麗許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, bingxu year, Goryeo sent envoys Heihuan and Fangshi to congratulate him on his succession; Kangzong sent Peilu on a return mission and to pursue the earlier agreement to recover fugitive subjects. Goryeo agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, bingxu year, Goryeo sent Heihuan and Fangshi to congratulate Kangzong on his accession. Kangzong sent Peilu on a return mission to renew the earlier agreement for the return of fugitives, and Goryeo consented.

sentences.zh: 曰：「使使至境上受之。」

translations.literal: They said, "Let envoys come to the border to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo said the fugitives would be handed over at the frontier to awaiting envoys."

sentences.zh: 康宗以為信然，使完顏部阿聒、烏林答部勝昆往境上受之。

translations.literal: Kangzong believed this to be sincere and sent A'suo of the Wanyan division and Shengkun of the Ulinada division to the border to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong took them at their word and sent A'suo of the Wanyan clan and Shengkun of the Ulinada clan to the border to receive the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 康宗畋于馬紀嶺乙只村以待之。

translations.literal: Kangzong hunted at Yizhi Village on Maji Ridge to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong went hunting at Yizhi Village on Maji Ridge to await their return.

sentences.zh: 阿聒、勝昆至境上，高麗遣人殺之，而出兵曷懶甸，築九城。

translations.literal: When A'suo and Shengkun reached the border, Goryeo sent men to kill them, and also dispatched troops to the Halin district, building nine fortified cities.
translations.idiomatic: When A'suo and Shengkun reached the frontier, Goryeo had them killed, sent troops into the Halin district, and built nine fortified towns.

sentences.zh: 康宗歸，眾鹹曰：「不可舉兵也，恐遼人將以罪我。」

translations.literal: When Kangzong returned, the multitude all said, "We must not raise troops, for fear the Liao people will hold it against us."
translations.idiomatic: On Kangzong's return, his advisers all urged, "We must not go to war—the Liao will hold us accountable."

sentences.zh: 太祖獨曰：「若不舉兵，豈止失曷懶甸，諸部皆非吾有也。」

translations.literal: The Taizu alone said, "If we do not raise troops, we will lose not only the Halin district—all the tribes will no longer be ours."
translations.idiomatic: The future Taizu alone objected: "If we do not fight, we will lose not only Halin—every tribe will slip from our grasp."

sentences.zh: 康宗以為然，乃使斡塞將兵伐之，大破高麗兵。

translations.literal: Kangzong agreed and thereupon sent Wosai to lead troops against them, inflicting a great defeat on the Goryeo army.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong was persuaded and sent Wosai at the head of an army. He routed the Goryeo forces.

sentences.zh: 六月，高麗率眾來戰，斡塞敗之，進圍其城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Goryeo led its masses to give battle; Wosai defeated them and advanced to besiege their city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Goryeo brought its main force to battle. Wosai defeated them and laid siege to their city.

sentences.zh: 七月，高麗複請和，康宗曰：「事若酌中，則與之和。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month Goryeo again requested peace. Kangzong said, "If the matter can be weighed to the middle ground, then make peace with them."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Goryeo sued for peace again. Kangzong said, "If the terms are fair, grant them peace."

sentences.zh: 高麗許歸亡入之民，罷九城之戍，複所侵故地，遂與之和。

translations.literal: Goryeo promised to return the subjects who had fled inward, to abandon the garrisons of the nine cities, and to restore the formerly seized lands, and thereupon peace was made.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo agreed to return the fugitives, dismantle the nine frontier garrisons, and restore seized territory, and peace was concluded.

sentences.zh: 收國元年九月，太祖已克黃龍府，命加古撒喝攻保州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Shouguo, the Taizu had already taken Huanglong Prefecture and ordered Jagusa to attack Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first Shouguo year, after Taizu had taken Huanglong Prefecture, he ordered Jagusa to attack Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 保州近高麗，遼侵高麗置保州。

translations.literal: Bozhou was near Goryeo; the Liao had invaded Goryeo and established Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou lay near Goryeo; the Liao had carved it out during their invasion of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 至是，命撒喝取之，久不下，撒喝請濟師，且言高麗王將遣使來。

translations.literal: At this time he ordered Saha to take it, but it was long untaken. Saha requested reinforcements and also reported that the king of Goryeo would send envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu now ordered Saha to capture it, but the siege dragged on. Saha asked for reinforcements and reported that the Goryeo king was about to send envoys.

sentences.zh: 太祖使納合烏蠢以百騎益之，詔撒喝曰：「汝領偏師，屢破重敵，多所俘獲，及聞胡沙數戰有功，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Nahe Wuchun with a hundred horsemen to reinforce him and issued an edict to Saha, saying, "You command a detached force and have repeatedly defeated powerful enemies, capturing many. I have also heard that Husha has been effective in several battles. I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Nahe Wuchun with a hundred cavalry as reinforcements and instructed Saha: "You have led a detached force, repeatedly defeated strong enemies, and taken many captives. I have also heard that Husha has distinguished himself in battle. I am greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 若保州未下，但守邊戍，吾已克黃龍府，聞遼主且至，俟破大敵複益汝兵。

translations.literal: If Bozhou is not yet taken, simply hold the border garrisons. I have already taken Huanglong Prefecture and have heard that the Liao ruler is about to arrive; after we defeat the great enemy I will again augment your troops.
translations.idiomatic: If Bozhou still holds out, hold the frontier posts. I have taken Huanglong Prefecture and hear the Liao emperor is coming. Once we defeat him I will send you more troops.

sentences.zh: 所言高麗遣使事，未知果否，至則護送以來。

translations.literal: As for what you report about Goryeo sending envoys, it is not yet known whether this is true; when they arrive, escort them here.
translations.idiomatic: As for Goryeo's promised envoys, that remains to be seen—when they arrive, escort them to me.

sentences.zh: 邊境之事，慎之毋忽。」

translations.literal: Border affairs—be cautious and do not neglect them."
translations.idiomatic: Be vigilant in all frontier matters—neglect nothing."

sentences.zh: 十一月，系遼女直麻懣太彎等十五人皆降，攻開州取之，盡降保州諸部女直。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, fifteen Liao Jurchen including Maman Taiwan were all bound and submitted; they attacked Kaizhou and took it, and all the Jurchen divisions of Bozhou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month fifteen Liao Jurchen leaders including Maman Taiwan surrendered. Kaizhou was taken by assault, and every Jurchen band around Bozhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 太祖以撒喝為保州路都統。

translations.literal: The Taizu appointed Saha commander-in-chief of the Bozhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu appointed Saha supreme commander of the Bozhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太祖已破走遼主軍，撒喝破合主、順化二城，複請濟師攻保州，使斡魯以甲士千人往。

translations.literal: The Taizu had already routed the Liao emperor's army. Saha took the two cities of Hezhu and Shunhua, again requested reinforcements to attack Bozhou, and the Taizu sent Wolu with a thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu had routed the Liao emperor's army, Saha captured Hezhu and Shunhua and again asked for troops to take Bozhou. Taizu sent Wolu with a thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 二年閏月，高麗遣使來賀捷，且曰：「保州本吾舊地，願以見還。」

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the second year, Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate him on the victory and also said, "Bozhou was originally our old territory; we wish it to be returned to us."
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of the second year, Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate Taizu on his victory and asked that Bozhou, "our former territory," be restored."

sentences.zh: 太祖謂使者曰：「爾其自取之。」

translations.literal: The Taizu said to the envoys, "You may take it yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told the envoys, "You may take it yourselves."

sentences.zh: 詔撒喝、烏蠢等曰：「若高麗來取保州，益以胡剌古、習顯等軍備之，或欲合兵，無得輒往，但謹守邊戍。」

translations.literal: He issued an edict to Saha, Wuchun, and the others, saying, "If Goryeo comes to take Bozhou, reinforce them with the armies of Hulagu, Xixian, and the like to prepare them. If they wish to combine forces, you are not to go rashly; simply guard the border posts carefully."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Saha, Wuchun, and the rest: "If Goryeo comes for Bozhou, supply them with Hulagu's, Xixian's, and other forces as needed. If they ask to join operations, do not rush in—only hold the frontier posts firmly."

sentences.zh: 及撒喝、阿實賚等攻保州，遼守將遁去，而高麗兵已在城中。

translations.literal: When Saha, Ashizai, and the others attacked Bozhou, the Liao defending general fled, but Goryeo troops were already inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Saha and Ashizai attacked Bozhou, the Liao garrison fled—but Goryeo troops were already inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 既而，高麗國王使蒲馬請保州，詔諭高麗王曰：「保州近爾邊境，聽爾自取，今乃勤我師徒，破敵城下。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the king of Goryeo sent Puma to request Bozhou. An edict addressed the king of Goryeo, saying, "Bozhou lies near your border; I allowed you to take it yourselves. Yet now you have mobilized my troops and broken the enemy beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Goryeo king sent Puma to claim Bozhou. Taizu's reply read: "Bozhou lies on your frontier and I let you take it yourself. Instead you drew my army in to fight beneath its walls.

sentences.zh: 且蒲馬止是口陳，俟有表請，即當別議。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Puma has only made an oral request; when there is a formal memorial petition, then another discussion may be held."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Puma spoke only orally. When a formal written petition arrives, we may discuss the matter further."

sentences.zh: 天輔二年十二月，詔諭高麗國王曰：「朕始興師伐遼，已嘗佈告，賴皇天助順，屢敗敵兵，北自上京，南至於海，其間京府州縣部族人民悉皆撫定。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Tianfu, an edict addressed the king of Goryeo, saying, "When I first raised troops to attack the Liao, I already proclaimed it. Relying on Heaven's assistance in accord with the right, I have repeatedly defeated the enemy's armies. From Shangjing in the north to the sea in the south, among all the capitals, prefectures, districts, tribes, and people in between, all have been pacified and settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianfu 2, Taizu notified the Goryeo king: "When I first marched against the Liao I made my intentions known. Heaven has favored the just cause, and I have repeatedly routed the enemy. From Shangjing in the north to the sea in the south, every capital, prefecture, district, tribe, and people in between has been brought under control.

sentences.zh: 今遣孛堇朮孛報諭，仍賜馬一匹，至可領也。」

translations.literal: Now I send the commander Zhushu to report and notify you, and also bestow one horse, which you may receive upon arrival."
translations.idiomatic: I now send Commander Zhushu with this notice and a gift of one horse—please accept them on his arrival."

sentences.zh: 三年，高麗增築長城三尺，邊吏發兵止之，弗從，報曰：「修補舊城。」

translations.literal: In the third year, Goryeo raised its Great Wall by three feet. Border officials sent troops to stop them, but they did not obey and reported, "We are repairing the old wall."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Goryeo raised its Great Wall by three feet. Jin border officials sent troops to stop the work, but Goryeo refused and replied that they were merely repairing the old wall.

sentences.zh: 曷懶甸孛堇胡剌古、習顯以聞，詔曰：「毋得侵軼生事，但慎固營壘，廣布耳目而已。」

translations.literal: The commanders Hulagu and Xixian of the Halin district reported this. An edict said, "You must not invade or provoke trouble; only carefully secure your camps and widely deploy scouts."
translations.idiomatic: Halin commanders Hulagu and Xixian reported the incident. The court ordered: "Do not raid or provoke incidents—only strengthen your camps and extend your intelligence network."

sentences.zh: 四年，咸州路都統司以兵分屯於保州、畢里圍二城，請益兵，詔曰：「汝等分列屯戍，以固封守，甚善。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the supreme command of the Xianzhou Circuit stationed troops separately at the two cities of Bozhou and Bilwei, and requested additional troops. An edict said, "Your separate garrison deployments to strengthen border defense are very good.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Xianzhou Circuit command split forces between Bozhou and Bilwei and asked for reinforcements. The response praised their dispersed garrison as sound frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 高麗累世臣事於遼，或有交通，可常遣人偵伺。」

translations.literal: Goryeo for generations served the Liao as vassal; there may be communications between them. You may regularly send men to spy and observe."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo served the Liao for generations and may still be in contact—keep scouts watching at all times."

sentences.zh: 使習顯以獲遼國州郡諭高麗，其國方誅亂者，使謂習顯曰：「此與先父國王之書。」

translations.literal: The envoy Xixian used the captured Liao prefectures and districts to notify Goryeo. That state was at the time executing those involved in disorder. The envoy said to Xixian, "This is a letter from my late father's reign."
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Xixian announced the Jin conquest of Liao prefectures to Goryeo, which was then purging rebels. A Goryeo official told Xixian, "This concerns my late father's reign."

sentences.zh: 習顯就館。

translations.literal: Xixian went to the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian withdrew to the guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 凡誅戮官僚七十余人，即依舊禮接見，而以表來賀，並貢方物。

translations.literal: In all, more than seventy officials were executed. Thereupon they received him according to the old ceremonies, and presented a memorial of congratulation together with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy officials were executed in the purge. Goryeo then received Xixian under the old ceremonial forms, sent a congratulatory memorial, and presented tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 複以遼帝亡入夏國報之。

translations.literal: They also reported that the Liao emperor had fled and entered the state of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: They also reported that the Liao emperor had fled into Western Xia territory.

sentences.zh: 高隨、斜野奉使高麗，至境上，接待之禮不遜，隨等不敢往，太宗曰：「高麗世臣於遼，當以事遼之禮事我，而我國有新喪，遼主未獲，勿遽強之。」

translations.literal: Gao Sui and Xieye were sent as envoys to Goryeo. At the border the reception ceremonies were not deferential; Sui and the others did not dare to proceed. Taizong said, "Goryeo for generations was vassal to the Liao and ought to serve me with the ceremonies used toward the Liao. But our state has a fresh bereavement, and the Liao ruler has not yet been captured—do not press them hastily."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sui and Xieye were sent to Goryeo, but at the frontier the reception was insufficiently deferential and they dared not enter. Taizong said, "Goryeo long served the Liao and should observe the same rites toward us—but the court is in mourning and the Liao emperor is not yet captured. Do not press them yet."

sentences.zh: 命高隨等還。

translations.literal: He ordered Gao Sui and the others to return.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gao Sui and his party to turn back.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，同知南路都統鶻實答奏，高麗納叛亡、增邊備，必有異圖。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui, the associate commander of the Southern Route, Heshida, memorialized that Goryeo was harboring defectors and fugitives and strengthening border defenses; it must harbor ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 2, Associate Southern Route Commander Heshida reported that Goryeo was sheltering defectors, strengthening frontier defenses, and likely harboring hostile intentions.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「凡有通問，毋違常式。

translations.literal: An edict said, "In all communications, do not depart from the usual forms.
translations.idiomatic: The court replied: "Maintain normal diplomatic exchanges in all communications.

sentences.zh: 或來侵略，則整爾行列與之從事。

translations.literal: If they come to invade, then array your ranks and engage them.
translations.idiomatic: If they invade, form your ranks and fight them.

sentences.zh: 敢先犯彼者，雖捷必罰。」

translations.literal: Whoever dares to strike them first, though victorious, will surely be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever strikes first, even if victorious, will be punished."

sentences.zh: 詔闍母以甲士千人戍海島，以備之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yanmu to garrison a thousand armored soldiers on the coastal islands as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmu was ordered to station a thousand armored men on the coastal islands as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 四年，國王王楷遣使奉表稱籓，優詔答之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, King Wang Kai of the state sent envoys presenting a memorial declaring himself a vassal; a gracious edict replied.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year King Wang Kai sent a memorial declaring vassalage, and the court answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 上使高伯淑、烏至忠使高麗，凡遣使往來當盡循遼舊，仍取保州路及邊地人口在彼界者，須盡數發還。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Gao Boshu and Wuzhizhong as envoys to Goryeo. All envoys sent back and forth should fully follow the old Liao practices, and moreover the population of the Bozhou Circuit and the borderlands who were on their side of the boundary must all be sent back in full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Gao Boshu and Wuzhizhong to Goryeo with orders that all future exchanges follow Liao precedent and that every subject of the Bozhou Circuit and border region held in Goryeo be returned in full.

sentences.zh: 敕伯淑曰：「若一一聽從，即以保州地賜之。」

translations.literal: He charged Boshu, saying, "If they obey in every particular, then grant them the territory of Bozhou."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Boshu: "If they comply fully, grant them the Bozhou territory."

sentences.zh: 高伯淑至高麗，王楷附表謝，一依事遼舊制。

translations.literal: When Gao Boshu reached Goryeo, Wang Kai appended a memorial of thanks, following entirely the old system used in serving the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: In Goryeo, Wang Kai sent a memorial of thanks pledging to follow the old Liao ceremonial system in full.

sentences.zh: 八年，楷上表，乞免索保州亡入邊戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Kai submitted a memorial requesting exemption from demanding the border households of Bozhou who had fled inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Wang Kai petitioned to be excused from surrendering the Bozhou fugitives who had crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高麗十人捕魚，大風飄其船抵海岸，曷蘇館人獲之，詔還其國。

translations.literal: That year, ten men of Goryeo were fishing when a great wind drove their boat to the coast; people of the Yisu Hall seized them, and an edict ordered them returned to their country.
translations.idiomatic: That year ten Goryeo fishermen were blown ashore by a storm. Yisu Hall people detained them, but an edict ordered their repatriation.

sentences.zh: 既而勖上表請不索保州亡入高麗戶口，太宗從之，自是保州封域始定。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Xu submitted a memorial requesting that the households of Bozhou who had fled inward to Goryeo not be demanded; Taizong consented, and from this time the territorial limits of Bozhou were first fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xu petitioned again to waive recovery of the Bozhou fugitives in Goryeo. Taizong agreed, and from then on the Bozhou frontier was fixed.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，詔加楷開府儀同三司、上柱國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong, an edict added to Kai the titles of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the Third Rank and Supreme Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 an edict conferred on Wang Kai the ranks of Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the Third Rank and Supreme Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 六年，楷薨，子晛嗣立。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Kai died, and his son Xian succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Wang Kai died and was succeeded by his son Xian.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，鴨綠江堡戍頗被侵越焚毀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading, the fortified posts along the Yalu River suffered considerable invasion, crossing of boundaries, burning, and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 4 the Yalu River frontier posts suffered repeated raids, incursions, and burning.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，世宗因正旦使朝辭，諭之曰：「邊境小小不虞，爾主使然邪，疆吏為之邪？

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Shizong, on the occasion of the New Year's envoy taking leave after audience, instructed him, saying, "Small mishaps on the border—did your lord cause them, or was it the frontier officials?
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, when the New Year's envoy took leave of Shizong, the emperor asked, "These minor frontier incidents—did your king order them, or were they the work of local officials?

sentences.zh: 若果疆吏為之，爾主亦當懲戒之也。」

translations.literal: If it was truly the frontier officials who did it, your lord should also punish and discipline them."
translations.idiomatic: If frontier officials are to blame, your king should discipline them as well."

sentences.zh: 初，高麗使者別有私進禮物以為常，是歲萬春節，上以使者私進不應典禮，詔罷之。

translations.literal: Formerly Goryeo envoys had separate private presentation gifts that had become customary. That year, at the Ten Thousand Springs festival, the emperor considered the envoys' private presentations not in accord with proper ceremony and issued an edict abolishing them.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo envoys had long brought private gifts in addition to official tribute. That year, at the Ten Thousand Springs festival, Shizong ruled these private offerings improper and abolished them by edict.

sentences.zh: 十年，王晛弟翼陽公皓廢晛自立。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Wang Xian's younger brother, the Duke of Yiyang, Hao, deposed Xian and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Wang Xian's younger brother, Duke Hao of Yiyang, deposed him and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 十月，賜生日使、大宗正丞颭至界上，高麗邊吏稱前王已讓位，不肯受使者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the birthday-congratulation envoy, the vice director of the Imperial Clan Court Zhan, reached the border. Goryeo border officials said the former king had already abdicated and refused to receive the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the birthday envoy Zhan, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, reached the frontier. Goryeo border officials cited the former king's abdication and refused to admit him.

sentences.zh: 十一年三月，王皓以讓國來奏告，詔婆速路勿受，有司移文詳問。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eleventh year, Wang Hao came to memorialize and report his cession of the state. An edict ordered the Basu Route not to receive him; the relevant offices sent documents to inquire in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eleventh year Wang Hao memorialized to announce his abdication. The court ordered the Basu Route not to receive him and instructed the relevant offices to send formal inquiries.

sentences.zh: 高麗告曰：「前王久病，昏耄不治，以母弟皓權攝國事。」

translations.literal: Goryeo reported, saying, "The former king has long been ill, senile and unable to govern, and has had his younger brother by the same mother, Hao, exercise regency over state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo reported that the former king had long been gravely ill and senile, unable to govern, and had entrusted state affairs to his uterine younger brother Hao as regent.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「讓國大事也，何以不先陳請。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The cession of a state is a great matter—why was it not reported and requested beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Abdication is a matter of the highest importance. Why was it not announced and requested in advance?"

sentences.zh: 詔有司再詳問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to inquire again in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the relevant offices to investigate further.

sentences.zh: 高麗乃以王晛讓國表來，大略稱先臣楷遺訓傳位於弟，又言其子有罪不可立之意。

translations.literal: Goryeo thereupon sent Wang Xian's memorial of cession of the state, which in general terms stated that the late subject Kai's testamentary instruction was to pass the throne to his younger brother, and also expressed the idea that his son was guilty and unfit to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo then submitted Wang Xian's abdication memorial, claiming broadly that the late King Kai's testament directed the throne to his brother and that his son was guilty and unfit to rule.

sentences.zh: 上疑之，以問宰執，丞相良弼奏曰：「此不可信。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious and asked the chief ministers. The chief councilor Liangbi memorialized, saying, "This cannot be believed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was skeptical and consulted his chief ministers. Chief Councilor Liangbi replied, "This cannot be credited.

sentences.zh: 晛止一子，往年生孫，嘗有表自陳生孫之喜，一也。

translations.literal: Xian has only one son; in a previous year a grandson was born, and there was once a memorial in which he himself reported the joy of a grandson's birth—that is the first point.
translations.idiomatic: First, Xian has only one son, and only last year a grandson was born—Xian himself once memorialized his joy at the birth.

sentences.zh: 皓嘗作亂，晛囚之，二也。

translations.literal: Hao once raised a rebellion and Xian imprisoned him—that is the second point.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Hao once rebelled and Xian had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 今晛不遣使，皓乃遣使，三也。

translations.literal: Now Xian sends no envoy, but Hao sends envoys—that is the third point.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Xian sends no envoys while Hao does.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賜晛生日使，皓不轉達於晛，乃稱未敢奉受，四也。

translations.literal: The court bestowed a birthday-congratulation envoy on Xian, but Hao did not forward him to Xian and instead said he dared not accept—that is the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, when the court sent a birthday envoy for Xian, Hao refused to forward him and claimed he dared not accept the mission.

sentences.zh: 今皓篡兄誣于天子，安可忍也。」

translations.literal: Now Hao has usurped his elder brother and deceived the Son of Heaven—how can this be endured?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Hao has seized the throne from his brother and deceived the Son of Heaven. This cannot be tolerated."

sentences.zh: 右丞孟浩曰：「當詢彼國士民，果皆推服，即當遣使封冊。」

translations.literal: The right vice councilor Meng Hao said, "We ought to inquire of that state's officials and people; if they truly all defer to him, then we should send envoys to invest him with the seal and patent."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Councilor Meng Hao argued, "We should inquire whether the Goryeo officials and people truly accept him. If they do, we may send envoys to invest him."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「封一國之君詢於民眾，此與除拜猛安謀克何異。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "To invest the ruler of a state after inquiring of the common people—how is this different from appointing and removing meng'an and mouke?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor objected, "Consulting the populace before investing a foreign king—how is that different from appointing meng'an and mouke officers?"

sentences.zh: 乃卻其使者，而以詔書詳問王晛，吏部侍郎靖為宣問王晛使。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent back their envoys and, with an imperial edict, made detailed inquiry of Wang Xian. Jing, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, served as envoy to announce the inquiry to Wang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Goryeo envoys back and dispatched Jing, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, with an edict to question Wang Xian directly.

sentences.zh: 皓實篡國，囚晛於海島。

translations.literal: Hao had in fact usurped the state and imprisoned Xian on a coastal island.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had in fact seized power and imprisoned Xian on a coastal island.

sentences.zh: 靖至高麗，皓稱王晛已避位出居他所，病加無損，不能就位拜命，往復險遠，非使者所宜往。

translations.literal: When Jing reached Goryeo, Hao said that Wang Xian had already yielded the throne and was living elsewhere, that his illness was growing worse without improvement, that he could not come to his post to receive the command, and that the journey back and forth was perilous and distant—not suitable for an envoy to undertake.
translations.idiomatic: In Goryeo, Hao claimed that Xian had abdicated and retired elsewhere, that his illness was worsening, that he could not come forward to receive the imperial message, and that the route was too dangerous and remote for an envoy.

sentences.zh: 靖竟不得見晛，乃以詔授皓，轉取晛表附奏，其言與前表大概相同。

translations.literal: Jing in the end could not see Xian. He thereupon presented the edict to Hao, obtained Xian's memorial in turn and appended it to his report; its wording was largely the same as the earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jing never saw Xian. He delivered the edict to Hao, obtained Xian's memorial indirectly, and forwarded it—the wording matched the earlier petition.

sentences.zh: 靖還，上問大臣，皆曰：「晛表如此，可遂封之。」

translations.literal: When Jing returned, the emperor asked the great ministers, and all said, "Since Xian's memorial is thus, we may proceed to invest him."
translations.idiomatic: On Jing's return the emperor consulted his ministers, who all urged, "Given Xian's memorial, we should proceed with the investiture."

sentences.zh: 丞相良弼、平章政事守道曰：「待皓祈請未晚也。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Liangbi and the privy councilor Shoudao said, "It is not too late to wait until Hao petitions and requests it."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Liangbi and Privy Councilor Shoudao dissented: "Let us wait until Hao himself petitions—it is not too late."

sentences.zh: 十二月，皓遣其禮部侍郎張翼明等請封。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Hao sent his vice director of the Ministry of Rites Zhang Yiming and others to request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hao sent Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yiming and others to request formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，遂賜封冊。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, the seal and patent of investiture were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year the court granted the investiture patent.

sentences.zh: 皓生日在正月十九日，是歲十二月將盡，未及遣使，有司請至來歲舉行焉。

translations.literal: Hao's birthday was on the nineteenth day of the first month; that year the twelfth month was nearly ended and envoys had not yet been dispatched. The relevant offices requested that it be carried out the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's birthday fell on the nineteenth of the first month. With the year nearly over, the relevant offices asked to defer the birthday mission until the following year.

sentences.zh: 十五年，高麗西京留守趙位寵叛皓，遣徐彥等九十六人上表曰：「前王本非避讓，大將軍鄭沖夫、郎將李義方實弑之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Zhao Weichong, military governor of Goryeo's Western Capital, rebelled against Hao and sent Xu Yan and ninety-six others with a memorial, saying, "The former king did not in fact abdicate; Grand General Zheng Chongfu and Colonel Li Yifang actually assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Zhao Weichong, Goryeo's Western Capital military governor, rebelled against Hao. Xu Yan and ninety-five others submitted a memorial claiming the former king had not abdicated but had been murdered by Grand General Zheng Chongfu and Colonel Li Yifang.

sentences.zh: 臣位寵請以慈悲嶺以西至鴨綠江四十餘城內屬，請兵助援。」

translations.literal: Your subject Weichong requests that more than forty cities from west of Cibei Ridge to the Yalu River be brought within our allegiance, and requests troops to assist."
translations.idiomatic: Weichong offered to submit more than forty cities west of Cibei Ridge to the Yalu River and asked for military aid.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「王皓已加封冊，位寵輒敢稱兵為亂，且欲納土，朕懷撫萬邦，豈助叛臣為虐。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "King Hao has already received investiture. Weichong dares to raise troops in rebellion and moreover wishes to surrender territory. I cherish and pacify the myriad states—how could I aid a rebellious minister in his cruelty?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "King Hao has already been invested. Weichong dares to rebel and offer territory. I cherish all states under Heaven—how could I aid a rebel in his violence?"

sentences.zh: 詔執徐彥等送高麗。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Xu Yan and the others be seized and sent to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xu Yan and his party seized and handed over to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 頃之，王皓定趙位寵之亂，遣使奏謝，自位寵之亂，皓所遣生日回謝、橫賜回謝、賀正旦、進奉、萬春節等使，皆阻不通，至是，皓並奏之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, King Hao put down Zhao Weichong's rebellion and sent envoys to memorialize thanks. Since Weichong's rebellion, the missions Hao had sent for birthday congratulations and return thanks, transverse bestowals and return thanks, New Year's congratulations, tribute presentations, and the Ten Thousand Springs festival had all been blocked and unable to pass. At this time Hao reported all of this together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hao suppressed Zhao Weichong's revolt and sent envoys with thanks. He also reported that since the rebellion his birthday, return-thanks, New Year's, tribute, and Ten Thousand Springs missions had all been blocked—he now listed them together.

sentences.zh: 詔答其意，其合遣人使令節次入朝。

translations.literal: An edict acknowledged his meaning and ordered that the envoys who ought to be sent should come to court in proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged his report and instructed that the due missions proceed to court in proper order.

sentences.zh: 十七年，賀正旦禮物，玉帶乃石似玉者，有司請移問，上曰：「彼小國無能識者，誤以為玉耳，不必移問。」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, among the New Year's congratulatory gifts, the jade belt was in fact stone resembling jade. The relevant offices requested a formal inquiry. The emperor said, "That small state has no one able to distinguish—it was mistakenly taken for jade. There is no need for a formal inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the New Year's gifts included a belt of stone that resembled jade. Officials proposed a formal inquiry, but the emperor said, "That small state lacks experts—they mistook stone for jade. No inquiry is needed."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十二月，有司奏高麗下節押馬官順成例外將帶甲三過界，上以使人所坐罪重，但令發還本國而已。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the relevant offices reported that during the lower festival, the horse-escort officer Shunchengwei led three armored men across the border in violation of regulations. The emperor considered the envoy's offense grave but ordered only that they be sent back to their own country.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month officials reported that during the lower festival Goryeo's horse-escort officer Shunchengwei had led three armed men across the border. Though the offense was serious, the emperor ordered only their repatriation.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，皓母任氏薨，皓乞免賜生日及賀謝等事，詔從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Hao's mother, Lady Ren, died. Hao requested exemption from birthday bestowals and congratulatory thanks and the like; an edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Hao's mother Lady Ren died. Hao asked to be excused from birthday gifts and congratulatory exchanges, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，皓表自陳衰病，以國讓其弟镡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengan, Hao submitted a memorial stating his own decline and illness and ceding the state to his younger brother Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan 2 Hao memorialized that he was aged and ill and ceded the throne to his younger brother Chan.

sentences.zh: 镡權國事。

translations.literal: Chan exercised regency over state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chan assumed regency.

sentences.zh: 是歲，皓廢，镡嗣立。

translations.literal: That year Hao was deposed and Chan succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hao was deposed and Chan ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年正月乙丑朔，高麗傔人以小佩刀割梨廡下巡廊，奉職見而糾之，詔館伴官自今前期移文禁止。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month, yichou day, in the fourth year of Taihe, a Goryeo attendant used a small waist knife to cut pears beneath the corridor of the side hall. A palace attendant saw this and reported it. An edict ordered the host officials that from now on they should send advance documents forbidding such acts.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, Taihe 4, a Goryeo attendant cut pears in the corridor with a small knife. A palace officer reported him, and the court ordered host officials to send advance notices forbidding such conduct.

sentences.zh: 是歲，王镡薨，子韺嗣立。

translations.literal: That year King Chan died and his son Ting succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Chan died and was succeeded by his son Ting.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年正月，是時用兵伐宋，夏亦有故，獨高麗遣正旦使，詔不賜曲宴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Taihe, at this time troops were being used to attack the Song, and Xia also had its reasons; Goryeo alone sent a New Year's envoy. An edict ordered that no curved banquet be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taihe 7 the court was at war with the Song and had business with Xia. Only Goryeo sent a New Year's envoy, and the court declined to grant the customary curved banquet.

sentences.zh: 及天壽節，夏、高麗使者皆在，有司奏：「大定初，宋未請和，夏、高麗使者賜曲宴，今請依大定故事。」

translations.literal: At the Heavenly Longevity festival, envoys from Xia and Goryeo were both present. The relevant offices memorialized, "At the beginning of Dading, when the Song had not yet sued for peace, envoys from Xia and Goryeo were granted curved banquets. We request that the Dading precedent be followed."
translations.idiomatic: At the Heavenly Longevity festival envoys from both Xia and Goryeo were present. Officials cited the early Dading precedent, when curved banquets were granted despite war with the Song, and asked to follow it.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年八月，王祦薨，嗣子未行起複。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhiyuan, King Ting died; the heir had not yet undertaken the resumption of mourning duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhiyuan 1 King Ting died before his heir had completed the mourning resumption rites.

sentences.zh: 九月，宣宗即位，邊吏奏：「高麗牒稱，嗣子未起複，不可以凶服迎吉詔，又不可以草土名銜署表。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Xuanzong ascended the throne. Border officials reported, "Goryeo's dispatch states that the heir has not resumed mourning, that he cannot receive an auspicious edict in mourning garb, and that he cannot sign a memorial with the title of one still in rough earth mourning."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, when Xuanzong ascended the throne, border officials reported that Goryeo claimed the heir had not resumed mourning and could neither receive the imperial edict in mourning dress nor sign memorials with a mourning title.

sentences.zh: 禮官議：「人臣不以私恩廢公義，宜權用吉服迎詔，署表用權國事名銜。

translations.literal: The ritual officials deliberated: "A subject must not set aside public duty because of private affection. He should provisionally use auspicious garb to receive the edict and sign the memorial with the title of one exercising regency over state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials ruled that private mourning must not override public duty: the heir should provisionally wear court dress to receive the edict and sign memorials as regent.

sentences.zh: 俟高麗告哀使至闕，然後遣使致祭、慰問及行封冊。」

translations.literal: Wait until Goryeo's mourning-announcement envoy reaches the court, and then dispatch envoys to offer sacrifices, express condolences, and carry out investiture."
translations.idiomatic: After Goryeo's mourning envoy reached the court, the Jin would send envoys for sacrifices, condolences, and investiture.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decision was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 明年，宣宗遷汴，遼東道路不通，興定三年，遼東行省奏高麗複有奉表朝貢之意，宰臣奏：「可令行省受其表章，其朝貢之禮俟他日徐議。」

translations.literal: The following year Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, and the roads through Liaodong were impassable. In the third year of Xingding, the Liaodong Branch Secretariat reported that Goryeo again had the intention of presenting memorials and coming to offer tribute. The chief ministers memorialized, "The Branch Secretariat may be ordered to receive their documents; the ceremonies of tribute presentation may be discussed slowly on another day."
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian and Liaodong routes were cut. In Xingding 3 the Liaodong Branch Secretariat reported renewed Goryeo interest in tribute. Ministers proposed accepting their documents now and deferring full ceremonial exchanges.

sentences.zh: 宣宗以為然，乃遣使撫諭高麗，終以道路不通，未遑迎迓，詔行省且羈縻勿絕其好，然自是不復通問矣。

translations.literal: Xuanzong agreed and thereupon sent envoys to comfort and instruct Goryeo, but in the end, because the roads were impassable, he had no leisure to receive them. An edict ordered the Branch Secretariat for the time being to keep them attached and not sever friendly relations, yet from this time onward communications ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong agreed and sent envoys to Goryeo, but impassable roads prevented a full reception. He ordered the Branch Secretariat to maintain ties without severing relations—but from then on regular contact ceased.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金人本出鞨靺之附於高麗者，始通好為鄰國，既而為君臣，貞祐以後道路不通，僅一再見而已。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: The people of Jin originally came from the Mohe who had attached themselves to Goryeo. At first they exchanged goodwill as neighboring states; afterward they became ruler and subject. After Zhenyou the roads were impassable, and they were seen only once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser observes: The Jin people originated among Mohe groups once subject to Goryeo. They began as neighbors, then became liege and vassal. After Zhenyou communications broke off, with only one or two further contacts.

sentences.zh: 入聖朝猶子孫相傳自為治，故不復備論，論其與金事相涉者焉。

translations.literal: Upon entering the sage dynasty they still governed themselves with succession from father to son, and therefore this is not further discussed in full; only matters involving Jin are discussed here.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present sage dynasty Goryeo still rules itself by hereditary succession, so no fuller account is given here—only matters touching Jin affairs.

sentences.zh: 金國語解

translations.literal: Explanation of the Language of the State of Jin
translations.idiomatic: Glossary of Jin State Language

sentences.zh: 今文《尚書》辭多奇澀，蓋亦當世之方言也。

translations.literal: The language of the present text of the Book of Documents is often strange and obscure; it too was probably the dialect of its own age.
translations.idiomatic: The present text of the 《Book of Documents》 is often obscure—likely the dialect of its own age.

sentences.zh: 《金史》所載本國之語，得諸重譯，而可解者何可闕焉。

translations.literal: The native language recorded in the 《History of Jin》, obtained through repeated translation, cannot be omitted where it can be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen terms preserved in the 《History of Jin》, though known only through repeated translation, should be recorded wherever they can be understood.

sentences.zh: 若其臣僚之小字，或以賤，或以疾，猶有古人尚質之風，不可文也。

translations.literal: As for the childhood names of their officials and ministers, some denoting low status, some denoting illness, they still preserve the ancient preference for plainness and cannot be ornamented with literary elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' childhood names—some denoting low birth, some illness—preserve an ancient plainness that should not be dressed in literary elegance.

sentences.zh: 國姓為某，漢姓為某，後魏孝文以來已有之矣。

translations.literal: The state surname being such-and-such and the Han surname being such-and-such—this has existed since Emperor Xiaowen of the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Dual state and Han surnames have existed since Emperor Xiaowen of the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 存諸篇終，以備考索。

translations.literal: They are preserved at the end of the chapters for reference and search.
translations.idiomatic: They are preserved at the end of this chapter for reference.

sentences.zh: 都勃極烈，總治官名，猶漢云「冢宰」。

translations.literal: Dubojilie: the title of the chief governing official, as the Han would say "Grand Minister."
translations.idiomatic: Dubojilie: chief governing title, equivalent to the Han "Grand Minister."

sentences.zh: 諳版勃極烈，官之尊且貴者。

translations.literal: Anban Bojilie: an office both honored and exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Anban Bojilie: a most honored and exalted office.

sentences.zh: 國論勃極烈，尊禮優崇得自由者。

translations.literal: Guolun Bojilie: one honored with ritual precedence and granted freedom of action.
translations.idiomatic: Guolun Bojilie: a councilor of high ritual standing who enjoyed special latitude.

sentences.zh: 胡魯勃極烈，統領官之稱。

translations.literal: Hulu Bojilie: the title of a commanding officer.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Bojilie: title of a commanding officer.

sentences.zh: 移賚勃極烈，位第三曰「移賚」。

translations.literal: Yicai Bojilie: the third rank is called "Yicai."
translations.idiomatic: Yicai Bojilie: the third rank, called "Yicai."

sentences.zh: 阿買勃極烈，治城邑者。

translations.literal: Amai Bojilie: one who administers walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: Amai Bojilie: administrator of walled cities.

sentences.zh: 乙室勃極烈，迎邪之官。

translations.literal: Yishi Bojilie: the office that receives and escorts envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Yishi Bojilie: office for receiving envoys.

sentences.zh: 劄失哈勃極烈，守官署之稱。

translations.literal: Zhashiha Bojilie: the title of one who guards the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhashiha Bojilie: title of one who guards government offices.

sentences.zh: 昃勃極烈，陰陽之官。

translations.literal: Ze Bojilie: the office of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Ze Bojilie: office of yin-yang divination.

sentences.zh: 迭勃極烈，倅貳之職。

translations.literal: Die Bojilie: the duty of a deputy second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: Die Bojilie: deputy second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 猛安，千夫長。

translations.literal: Meng'an: commander of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an: leader of a thousand-man unit.

sentences.zh: 謀克，百夫長也。

translations.literal: Mouke: commander of a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Mouke: leader of a hundred-man unit.

sentences.zh: 諸颭「詳穩」，邊戍之官。

translations.literal: Among the zhans, "Xiangwen": an office of frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Among frontier officers, "Xiangwen": a border defense post.

sentences.zh: 諸「移里堇」，部落墟砦之首領。

translations.literal: Among the "Yilijin": chiefs of tribal stockades and fortified hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: "Yilijin": chiefs of tribal stockades and fortified hamlets.

sentences.zh: 詳穩、移里堇，本遼語，金人因之而稍異同焉。

translations.literal: Xiangwen and Yilijin were originally Liao terms; the Jin adopted them with slight differences.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwen and Yilijin were originally Liao terms; the Jin adopted them with slight modifications.

sentences.zh: 禿里，掌部落詞訟，察非違者。

translations.literal: Tuli: in charge of tribal lawsuits and investigating violations.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli: overseer of tribal lawsuits and investigator of violations.

sentences.zh: 烏魯古，牧圉之官。

translations.literal: Wulugu: the office of herds and enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: Wulugu: officer of herds and enclosures.

sentences.zh: 斡里朵，官府治事之所。

translations.literal: Woliduo: the place where the government offices conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Woliduo: seat of government administration.

sentences.zh: 孛論出，胚胎之名。

translations.literal: Belunchu: the name for an embryo.
translations.idiomatic: Belunchu: term for an embryo.

sentences.zh: 阿胡迭，長子。

translations.literal: Ahudie: the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Ahudie: eldest son.

sentences.zh: 骨赧，季也。

translations.literal: Gunai: the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Gunai: youngest son.

sentences.zh: 蒲陽溫，曰幼子。

translations.literal: Puyangwen: called the young son.
translations.idiomatic: Puyangwen: the young son.

sentences.zh: 益都，次第之通稱。

translations.literal: Yidu: the general term for order of birth.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu: general term for birth order.

sentences.zh: 第九曰「烏也」，十六曰「女魯歡」。

translations.literal: The ninth is called "Wuye"; the sixteenth is called "Nülühuan."
translations.idiomatic: The ninth son is called "Wuye"; the sixteenth, "Nülühuan."

sentences.zh: 按答海，客之通稱。

translations.literal: Andahai: the general term for a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Andahai: general term for a guest.

sentences.zh: 山只昆，舍人也。

translations.literal: Shanzhikun: a retainer.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhikun: retainer.

sentences.zh: 散亦孛，奇男子。

translations.literal: Sanyibo: an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyibo: extraordinary man.

sentences.zh: 散答，老人之稱也。

translations.literal: Sanda: a term for an old man.
translations.idiomatic: Sanda: term for an old man.

sentences.zh: 什古乃，瘠人。

translations.literal: Shigunai: a lean person.
translations.idiomatic: Shigunai: lean person.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦，黧黑之名。

translations.literal: Sahelian: a name for dark black.
translations.idiomatic: Sahelian: term for dark black.

sentences.zh: 保活里，侏儒。

translations.literal: Baohuoli: a dwarf.
translations.idiomatic: Baohuoli: dwarf.

sentences.zh: 阿里孫，貌不揚也。

translations.literal: Alisun: one whose appearance is not striking.
translations.idiomatic: Alisun: one of unremarkable appearance.

sentences.zh: 阿徒罕，采薪之子。

translations.literal: Atuhan: a son who gathers firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Atuhan: firewood gatherer.

sentences.zh: 答不也，耘田者。

translations.literal: Dabuye: one who tills the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Dabuye: field tiller.

sentences.zh: 阿土古，善採捕者。

translations.literal: Atugu: one skilled at gathering and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Atugu: skilled hunter-gatherer.

sentences.zh: 阿里喜，圍獵也。

translations.literal: Alixi: encircling hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Alixi: a driven hunt with encirclement.

sentences.zh: 拔里速，角牴戲者。

translations.literal: Balisu: one who performs wrestling contests.
translations.idiomatic: Balisu: wrestler.

sentences.zh: 阿離合懣，臂鷹鶻者。

translations.literal: Aliheman: one who carries a hawk or falcon on the arm.
translations.idiomatic: Aliheman: falconer.

sentences.zh: 胡魯剌，戶長。

translations.literal: Hulula: head of a household.
translations.idiomatic: Hulula: household head.

sentences.zh: 阿合，人奴也。

translations.literal: Ahe: a human slave.
translations.idiomatic: Ahe: human slave.

sentences.zh: 兀朮，曰頭。

translations.literal: Wuzhu: called the head.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu: means "head."

sentences.zh: 粘罕，心也。

translations.literal: Nianhan: the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan: means "heart."

sentences.zh: 畏可，牙，又曰吾亦可。

translations.literal: Weike: the tooth; also called wuyike.
translations.idiomatic: Weike: tooth; also called wuyike.

sentences.zh: 盤里合，將指。

translations.literal: Panlihe: the general's finger.
translations.idiomatic: Panlihe: the general's finger.

sentences.zh: 三合，人之靨也。

translations.literal: Sanhe: a person's dimple.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe: dimple.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔，瘍瘡。

translations.literal: Yawuta: ulcer and sore.
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta: ulcer or sore.

sentences.zh: 蒲剌都，目赤而盲也。

translations.literal: Puladu: red-eyed and blind.
translations.idiomatic: Puladu: one with red eyes who is blind.

sentences.zh: 石哥里，溲疾。

translations.literal: Shigel: urinary ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Shigel: urinary disorder.

sentences.zh: 謾都謌，癡騃之謂。

translations.literal: Manduge: a term for stupidity and dullness.
translations.idiomatic: Manduge: term for dull-wittedness.

sentences.zh: 謀良虎，無賴之名。

translations.literal: Moulianghu: a name for a rascal.
translations.idiomatic: Moulianghu: term for a rascal.

sentences.zh: 皆不美之稱也。

translations.literal: All are unflattering designations.
translations.idiomatic: All of these are unflattering names.

sentences.zh: 與人同受福曰「忽都」。

translations.literal: Sharing blessing with others is called "Hudu."
translations.idiomatic: "Hudu": sharing good fortune with others.

sentences.zh: 以力助人曰「阿息保」。

translations.literal: Helping others with one's strength is called "Axibao."
translations.idiomatic: "Axibao": helping others by one's own strength.

sentences.zh: 辭不失，酒醒也。

translations.literal: Cibushi: sober from wine.
translations.idiomatic: Cibushi: sober after drinking.

sentences.zh: 奴申，和睦之義。

translations.literal: Nushen: the meaning of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Nushen: harmony, concord.

sentences.zh: 訛出虎，寬容之名也。

translations.literal: Echuhu: a name signifying forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Echuhu: a name denoting forbearance.

sentences.zh: 賽里，安樂。

translations.literal: Saili: peace and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Saili: peace and contentment.

sentences.zh: 迪古乃，來也。

translations.literal: Digunai: to come.
translations.idiomatic: Digunai: means "to come."

sentences.zh: 撒八，迅速之義。

translations.literal: Saba: the meaning of swiftness.
translations.idiomatic: Saba: swiftness, speed.

sentences.zh: 烏古出，方言曰再休，猶言再不復也。

translations.literal: Wuguchu: in the dialect called Zaixiu, as if to say "never again."
translations.idiomatic: Wuguchu: in dialect "Zaixiu," meaning "never again."

sentences.zh: 凡事之先者曰「石倫」。

translations.literal: Whatever comes first in any matter is called "Shilun."
translations.idiomatic: "Shilun": whatever comes first in any matter.

sentences.zh: 以物與人已然曰「阿里白」。

translations.literal: Having already given something to someone is called "Alibai."
translations.idiomatic: "Alibai": having already given something to someone.

sentences.zh: 吾里補，畜積之名。

translations.literal: Wulibu: a name for stored goods and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Wulibu: term for stored goods and livestock.

sentences.zh: 習失，猶人云常川也。

translations.literal: Xishi: as people say "constant flow."
translations.idiomatic: Xishi: as people say, "constant flow."

sentences.zh: 凡市物已得曰「兀帶」，取以名子者，猶言貨取如物然也。

translations.literal: Whenever goods in the market have been obtained it is called "Wudai"; taking this to name a child is as if to say acquiring goods like merchandise.
translations.idiomatic: "Wudai": goods obtained in trade; used as a child's name, it suggests acquiring goods as in commerce.

sentences.zh: 兀典，明星。

translations.literal: Wudian: bright star.
translations.idiomatic: Wudian: a bright star.

sentences.zh: 阿鄰，山。

translations.literal: Alin: mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Alin: means "mountain."

sentences.zh: 太神，高也。

translations.literal: Taishen: high.
translations.idiomatic: Taishen: high, lofty.

sentences.zh: 山之上銳者曰「哈丹」，坡陀曰「阿懶」，大而峻曰「斜魯」。

translations.literal: A mountain peak that is sharp is called "Hadan"; a sloping rise is called "Alan"; large and steep is called "Xielu."
translations.idiomatic: A sharp mountain peak is "Hadan"; a gentle slope, "Alan"; a large steep mountain, "Xielu."

sentences.zh: 忒鄰，海也。

translations.literal: Telin: the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Telin: means "the sea."

sentences.zh: 沙忽帶，舟也。

translations.literal: Shahudai: a boat.
translations.idiomatic: Shahudai: boat.

sentences.zh: 生鐵曰「斡論」，釜曰「闍母」，刃曰「斜烈」。

translations.literal: Wrought iron is called "Wolun"; a cauldron is called "Zhamu"; a blade is called "Xielie."
translations.idiomatic: Wrought iron: "Wolun"; cauldron: "Zhamu"; blade: "Xielie."

sentences.zh: 婆盧火者槌也。

translations.literal: Poluhuo is a mallet.
translations.idiomatic: Poluhuo: mallet.

sentences.zh: 金曰「桉春」。

translations.literal: Gold is called "Anchun."
translations.idiomatic: Gold: "Anchun."

sentences.zh: 銀朮可，珠也。

translations.literal: Yinzhuke: pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhuke: means "pearl."

sentences.zh: 布囊曰「蒲盧渾」，盆曰「阿里虎」，罐曰「活女」。

translations.literal: A cloth sack is called "Puluhun"; a basin is called "Alihu"; a jar is called "Huonü."
translations.idiomatic: Cloth sack: "Puluhun"; basin: "Alihu"; jar: "Huonü."

sentences.zh: 烏烈，草廩也。

translations.literal: Wulie: a hay granary.
translations.idiomatic: Wulie: hay granary.

sentences.zh: 沙剌，衣襟也。

translations.literal: Shala: the lapel of a garment.
translations.idiomatic: Shala: garment lapel.

sentences.zh: 活臘胡，色之赤者也。

translations.literal: Huolahu: the color red.
translations.idiomatic: Huolahu: red color.

sentences.zh: 胡剌，灶突。

translations.literal: Hula: the chimney opening of a stove.
translations.idiomatic: Hula: stove chimney opening.

sentences.zh: 桓端，松。

translations.literal: Huanduan: pine.
translations.idiomatic: Huanduan: pine tree.

sentences.zh: 阿虎里，松子。

translations.literal: Ahuli: pine nut.
translations.idiomatic: Ahuli: pine nuts.

sentences.zh: 孰輦，蓮也。

translations.literal: Shunian: lotus.
translations.idiomatic: Shunian: the lotus.

sentences.zh: 活離罕，羔。

translations.literal: Huolihan: lamb.
translations.idiomatic: Huolihan: a lamb.

sentences.zh: 合喜，犬子。

translations.literal: Hexi: puppy.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi: a young dog.

sentences.zh: 訛古乃，犬之有文者。

translations.literal: Egunei: a dog with markings.
translations.idiomatic: Egunei: a marked dog.

sentences.zh: 斜哥，貂鼠。

translations.literal: Xiege: sable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege: the sable.

sentences.zh: 蒲阿，山雞。

translations.literal: Pu'a: pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: Pu'a: the pheasant.

sentences.zh: 窩謀罕，鳥卵也。

translations.literal: Womouhan: bird's egg.
translations.idiomatic: Womouhan: a bird's egg.

sentences.zh: 完顏，漢姓曰王。

translations.literal: Wanyan: the Han surname is Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan clan: Han surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 烏古論曰商。

translations.literal: Wugulun is Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun clan: Han surname Shang.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈曰高。

translations.literal: Heshilie is Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Heshilie clan: Han surname Gao.

sentences.zh: 徒單曰杜。

translations.literal: Tudan is Du.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan clan: Han surname Du.

sentences.zh: 女奚烈曰郎。

translations.literal: Nüxilie is Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Nüxilie clan: Han surname Lang.

sentences.zh: 兀顏曰朱。

translations.literal: Wuyan is Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan clan: Han surname Zhu.

sentences.zh: 蒲察曰李。

translations.literal: Pucha is Li.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha clan: Han surname Li.

sentences.zh: 顏盞曰張。

translations.literal: Yanzhan is Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhan clan: Han surname Zhang.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕曰溫。

translations.literal: Wendihan is Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan clan: Han surname Wen.

sentences.zh: 石抹曰蕭。

translations.literal: Shimo is Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Shimo clan: Han surname Xiao.

sentences.zh: 奧屯曰曹。

translations.literal: Aotun is Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Aotun clan: Han surname Cao.

sentences.zh: 孛朮魯曰魯。

translations.literal: Bozhulu is Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhulu clan: Han surname Lu.

sentences.zh: 移剌曰劉。

translations.literal: Yila is Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Yila clan: Han surname Liu.

sentences.zh: 斡勒曰石。

translations.literal: Wole is Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Wole clan: Han surname Shi.

sentences.zh: 納剌曰康。

translations.literal: Nala is Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Nala clan: Han surname Kang.

sentences.zh: 夾谷曰仝。

translations.literal: Jiagu is Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagu clan: Han surname Tong.

sentences.zh: 裴滿曰麻。

translations.literal: Peiman is Ma.
translations.idiomatic: Peiman clan: Han surname Ma.

sentences.zh: 尼忙古曰魚。

translations.literal: Nimanggu is Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Nimanggu clan: Han surname Yu.

sentences.zh: 斡准曰趙。

translations.literal: Wozhun is Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wozhun clan: Han surname Zhao.

sentences.zh: 阿典曰雷。

translations.literal: Adian is Lei.
translations.idiomatic: Adian clan: Han surname Lei.

sentences.zh: 阿里侃曰何。

translations.literal: Alikan is He.
translations.idiomatic: Alikan clan: Han surname He.

sentences.zh: 溫敦曰空。

translations.literal: Wendun is Kong.
translations.idiomatic: Wendun clan: Han surname Kong.

sentences.zh: 吾魯曰惠。

translations.literal: Wulu is Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wulu clan: Han surname Hui.

sentences.zh: 抹顏曰孟。

translations.literal: Moyan is Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Moyan clan: Han surname Meng.

sentences.zh: 都烈曰強。

translations.literal: Dulie is Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dulie clan: Han surname Qiang.

sentences.zh: 散答曰駱。

translations.literal: Sanda is Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Sanda clan: Han surname Luo.

sentences.zh: 呵不哈曰田。

translations.literal: Hebuha is Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Hebuha clan: Han surname Tian.

sentences.zh: 烏林答曰蔡。

translations.literal: Ulinada is Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Ulinada clan: Han surname Cai.

sentences.zh: 僕散曰林。

translations.literal: Pusan is Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan clan: Han surname Lin.

sentences.zh: 朮虎曰董。

translations.literal: Shuhu is Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhu clan: Han surname Dong.

sentences.zh: 古里甲曰汪。

translations.literal: Gulijia is Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Gulijia clan: Han surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 其後氏族或因人變易，難以遍舉，姑載其可知者云。

translations.literal: Afterward clans and surnames sometimes changed with individuals, and it is difficult to list them all; here are recorded only those that can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Later, clan names sometimes shifted with individuals, making a full list impossible; only those known with certainty are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 金國語解終。

translations.literal: End of the Explanation of the Language of the State of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: End of the Glossary of Jin State Language.
